source_artifacts.locator: approval queue (as shown to the analyst)

capabilities.target: user's MFA methods and issuance of a temporary access pass
chat message to the ticket requester

inputs.source: Support ticket, including tickets emailed in by contractors and vendors

instructions.note: The instruction sends the temp pass to 'the person who opened the ticket' with no requirement to verify that person is the account owner. Runtime notes confirm the pass goes to the ticket opener, not the account owner, which is exploitable when tickets are emailed in by outside contractors/vendors.

autonomy.level is declared A2 (approval on sensitive actions) for the agent, but cap.send_temp_pass has no approval_gate_ref. Per rubric section 3, this capability is scored as A3 (act then report) rather than A2 for assessment purposes.

elements.name: Identity provider directory (user profiles and verified contact records)

controls.name: Service desk analyst approval in queue tool
controls.decay_rationale: Does not decay with model capability because the analyst reviews the raw target, requester, and full ticket text rather than a model-generated summary. It decays instead under approval volume (approval fatigue) and provides no independent verification that the self-reported requester field is the true account owner.

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to system of record (missing)
controls.decay_rationale: Would not decay with model capability because the destination would be pulled from the verified IdP directory record rather than from ticket content or model output.

controls.name: Approval gate on temp-pass delivery (missing)
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action approval gate on the send step itself would not decay with model capability; it is currently absent, so the send executes automatically once the reset is approved.

controls.name: Out-of-band requester identity verification (missing)
controls.decay_rationale: An out-of-band check (callback to a known number, or matching against a verified contractor registry) would not decay with model capability, since it does not rely on model- or ticket-presented content.

findings.title: TC4 confused deputy: raw-action approval gate cannot verify ticket requester identity before MFA reset

attack_path.note: Contractor/vendor-submitted ticket; the requester field is simply the email sender and is not independently verified.
Agent looks up the target user to prepare the reset.
Agent resets MFA after analyst approval; the approval reviews raw ticket content but has no way to confirm the requester's true identity.

findings.residual_rationale: The analyst approval is a raw-action gate on this sink, which mechanically credits -2 tiers (critical to moderate) with no floor restriction. We rate residual higher, at high, because the queue's only identity signal is the self-reported 'Requested by' field (the external email sender) with no independent identity proofing, and two analysts approve roughly 200 mostly-routine requests each per shift, which the mechanism/dependence classification alone does not capture.

forecast.watch_signal: autonomy.level for cap.mfa_reset is raised toward act-then-report, the approval_gate_ref is removed, or auto-approval/batch approval is introduced to clear queue backlog.

evidence.observation: Every reset needs analyst approval in the queue tool before it runs.
The queue shows Target, Requested by (the ticket requester), and the full ticket text, but no independent identity verification of the requester.
Contractors and vendors can email tickets in; the requester field is the email sender.
Two analysts cover the queue and approve about 400 requests per shift; most are routine.

recommendations.action: Add an out-of-band identity verification step (callback to a known contractor/employee number, or SSO-authenticated ticket submission) before an MFA reset ticket reaches the approval queue.
Flag and route to secondary review any reset request where the requester's email domain differs from the target user's organizational domain.

findings.title: Temp-pass delivery bypasses approval entirely: destination not bound to verified account owner

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled or spoofed ticket names itself as requester.
Reset is approved based on raw ticket review (see F1).
Temp pass is sent automatically to the ticket opener with no separate approval or destination verification.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: A new delivery channel (email, SMS) is added for the temp pass without destination binding, the ticket intake surface expands to more external submitters, or the existing analyst_approval gate is weakened further.

evidence.observation: The temporary pass goes to whoever opened the ticket, not to the account owner.
The queue entry's Action is listed only as idp.reset_mfa; chat.send_temp_pass is not a reviewed action.
send the temporary access pass to the person who opened the ticket

recommendations.action: Bind the temp-pass recipient to the account owner's verified contact in the IdP directory, never to the ticket's self-reported requester field.
Add a human approval gate (raw action) on chat.send_temp_pass itself, or extend the existing gate to require explicit review of the delivery destination before it runs.

rating.rationale: Two findings drive the rating. F1: an untrusted, contractor-emailable ticket can trigger an MFA reset (S3, credential_access); the sole control is a raw-action analyst approval gate, which earns the standard -2 tier credit but is overridden upward to high because the gate has no way to verify the self-reported requester's identity and runs under approval-fatigue conditions (~200 approvals/analyst/shift, mostly routine) -- a design fact the mechanism/dependence classification cannot express. F2: the resulting temporary access pass is delivered automatically to the ticket opener (cap.send_temp_pass, S3 egress of restricted credential material) with no approval gate and no binding to the verified account owner at all, so residual equals inherent at critical. The agent's autonomy is declared A2 (approval on sensitive actions), but cap.send_temp_pass has no approval_gate_ref; per rubric section 3 that capability is effectively A3 for this design, which is itself part of the gap. Forecast stays at critical for both findings: F1 would collapse further under autonomy_increase or control_removal of the one gate it has, and F2 is already unmitigated and would only worsen if new delivery channels or broader ticket sources are added. The single control whose decay matters most is ctl.analyst_approval -- it looks protective on paper but does not cover the actual exfiltration step and cannot verify the one fact (requester identity) the whole design depends on.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration shown in the artifacts, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No MCP/tool manifest, authentication configuration, or IdP schema was provided; credential_scope and maestro_layer values are inferred from the action descriptions, so confidence on those specific fields is medium.

autonomy.level is declared A2 for the agent overall, but cap.send_temp_pass has no approval_gate_ref; per rubric section 3 this capability was scored as A3 (act then report) for finding F2 rather than taking the A2 declaration at face value.
